newsitem.title: INDIA: First India launches 3-yr close-ended mutual fund.
newsitem.headline: First India launches 3-yr close-ended mutual fund.

text.p: The Madras-based First India Asset Management Company has launched a three-year close-ended mutual fund called First India TaxGain 1997.
"It will be a pure growth scheme," First India's fund manager P.Singaravelu told Reuters on Thursday.

About two-thirds of the fund will be invested in blue-chips, 15 to 20 percent in convertible debentures and the rest in stocks whose earnings growth would be higher than that of the market, Singaravelu said.
N.Subramanian, First India's chief executive officer, said the time was appropriate for investment in mutual funds.
He said he was looking forward to a risk-reward ratio of "15 percent downside and 50 percent upside."
First India Mutual Fund is a joint venture asset management company floated by First India Leasing Company of India and Guinness Flight Group, a U.K.-based fund manager.
First India is acting as the Indian investment advisor to an offshore-fund called "Madras Equity Fund" floated overseas by Guinness Flight in November 1995.
This fund has grown to about $14 million from an initial corpus of $3.0 million, the company said in a statement.
"Madras Equity Fund was ranked as the top performing India-specific fund by Micropal as of June 1996, and is among the top performing India funds to date," it said.

Investors in First India TaxGain 1997, which closes on March 31, 1997, will enjoy tax credit of 20 percent on the investment by them up to a maximum of 10,000 rupees under Section 88 of the Income Tax Act, it said.

Tax benefits would also accrue under Section 80L of the Income Tax Act on dividend upto a maximum of 15,000 rupees, with an exclusive deduction of 3,000 rupees on dividend income earned from mutual funds and Indian firms under Section 48, 54EB and 112 on capital gains, the firm said in a statement.
